extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and potential litigants or practitioners interested in federal transportation project decisions (FHWA/FDOT), including state DOT staff and environmental/legal counsel
extracted.subtask_short: FHWA notice of final agency actions
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register notice announcing final federal agency actions for a specific transportation project (Type 2 Categorical Exclusion), identifying applicable laws/regulations, where project documents may be found, and the deadline and legal limitations for seeking judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on claims / deadline for judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim seeking judicial review of the Federal Agency actions on the listed highway project will be barred unless the claim is filed on or before March 14, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Federal law that authorizes judicial review of a claim provides a time period of less than 150 days for filing such claim, then that shorter time period still applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice under 23 U.S.C. 139(l)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FHWA, on behalf of FDOT, is advising the public of final agency actions subject to 23 U.S.C. 139(l)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory authority is the basis for the limitation on claims described in the notice; the notice identifies the project actions covered as of the issuance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment status
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are no longer being accepted for this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See DATES for details; Regulations.gov data shown on FederalRegister.gov is additional context but not part of the official FR document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of project documents (Type 2 Categorical Exclusion and records)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Type 2 Categorical Exclusion and additional project documents are available on the project website or by contacting the FDOT Office of Environmental Management at the provided address during normal business hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project website: https://www.cflroads.com/project/446445-5. The notice states that the actions and the laws under which they were taken are described in the Type 2 Categorical Exclusion and other project records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information for inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: A named contact (Jennifer Marshall, P.E., Director, FDOT Office of Environmental Management) with telephone and email is provided for further information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact details: telephone (850) 414-4316; email Jennifer.Marshall@dot.state.fl.us.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment/assumption of environmental responsibilities (23 U.S.C. 327)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective dates of assignment/assumption of environmental responsibilities are provided (effective December 14, 2016, and renewed May 26, 2022), indicating FDOT assumed environmental responsibilities for this project pursuant to 23 U.S.C. 327.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the delegations of responsibility between FHWA and FDOT that underpin the environmental decisionmaking documented in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project description content (location and facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice specifies project location and the proposed facilities: Osceola County Site along CR 532, approximately 3.87 miles east of I-4 interchange; 234 truck parking spaces; centralized restroom building with restroom facilities, vending machines, and an office for security staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such descriptive elements are expected content in a project notice to identify the scope and nature of the action for purposes of legal notice and public awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of agency actions (licenses, permits, approvals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The actions described in the notice grant licenses, permits, or approvals for the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice applies to the Type 2 Categorical Exclusion and all other Federal Agency licenses, permits, or approvals for the listed project as of the issuance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) [42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq.] applies to the project and is among the laws under which actions were taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced regulatory implementing authority includes 23 CFR part 771; the notice identifies the Type 2 Categorical Exclusion as the NEPA-related document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal-Aid Highway Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal-Aid Highway Act (FAHA) [23 U.S.C. 109 and 23 U.S.C. 128] is listed among applicable laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes govern aspects of federal-aid highway projects and funding responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean Air Act considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean Air Act (CAA) [42 U.S.C. 7401-7671(q)] applies to the project, with the exception of project-level conformity determinations [42 U.S.C. 7506].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Air-related statutory requirements are recognized, but the notice explicitly excepts project-level conformity determinations from the cited applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noise requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Noise Control Act of 1972 [42 U.S.C. 4901-4918] and 23 CFR part 772 are listed as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noise impacts and compliance with applicable noise regulations are part of the environmental considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land use and Section 4(f) / LWCF protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4(f) of the Department of Transportation Act of 1966 [23 U.S.C. 138 and 49 U.S.C. 303]; 23 CFR part 774; and Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) [54 U.S.C. 200302-200310] apply where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protections for publicly owned parks, recreation lands, wildlife and waterfowl refuges, and historic sites are invoked under these authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wildlife and fishery statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Endangered Species Act (ESA) [16 U.S.C. 1531-1544 and 1536]; Marine Mammal Protection Act (MPPA) [16 U.S.C. 1361-1423h]; Anadromous Fish Conservation Act [16 U.S.C. 757(a)-757(f)]; Fish and Wildlife Coordination Act [16 U.S.C. 661-667(d)]; Migratory Bird Treaty Act (MBTA) [16 U.S.C. 703-712]; Magnuson-Stevenson Fishery Conservation and Management Act (MSA) [16 U.S.C. 1801-1891d] with Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) requirements [16 U.S.C. 1855(b)(2)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes identify biological resource considerations and consultation/mitigation obligations for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic and cultural resources laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) [54 U.S.C. 3006101 et seq.]; Archaeological Resources Protection Act (ARPA) [16 U.S.C. 470(aa)-470(II)]; Preservation of Historical and Archaeological Data [54 U.S.C. 312501-312508]; Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act (NAGPRA) [25 U.S.C. 3001-3013; 18 U.S.C. 1170] apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These authorities govern treatment, consultation, and protections for historic, archaeological, and Native American cultural resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and economic statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil Rights Act of 1964 [42 U.S.C. 2000d-2000d-1]; American Indian Religious Freedom Act (AIRFA) [42 U.S.C. 1996]; Farmland Protection Policy Act (FPPA) [7 U.S.C. 4201-4209] are listed as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes address nondiscrimination, protection of religious practices, and farmland protection considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wetlands and water resources laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean Water Act (CWA) (section 319, section 401, section 404) [33 U.S.C. 1251-1387]; Coastal Barriers Resources Act (CBRA) [16 U.S.C. 3501-3510]; Coastal Zone Management Act (CZMA) [16 U.S.C. 1451-1466]; Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) [42 U.S.C. 300f-300j-26]; Rivers and Harbors Act of 1899 [33 U.S.C. 401-406]; Wild and Scenic Rivers Act [16 U.S.C. 1271-1287]; Emergency Wetlands Resources Act [16 U.S.C. 3921, 3931]; Wetlands Mitigation [23 U.S.C. 119(g) and 133(b)(3)]; Flood Disaster Protection Act [42 U.S.C. 4001-4130].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These laws cover water quality, wetland protections, coastal and riverine resource protections, mitigation requirements, and floodplain considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazardous materials statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) [42 U.S.C. 9601-9675]; Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act (SARA); Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) [42 U.S.C. 6901-6992(k)] are listed as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes govern assessment and management of hazardous substances and contaminated sites in project planning and approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable Executive Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Orders invoked include: E.O. 11990 Protection of Wetlands; E.O. 11988 Floodplain Management; E.O. 12898 Federal Actions to Address Environmental Justice in Minority Populations and Low-Income Populations; E.O. 11593 Protection and Enhancement of Cultural Resources; E.O. 13007 Indian Sacred Sites; E.O. 13287 Preserve America; E.O. 11514 Protection and Enhancement of Environmental Quality; E.O. 13112 Invasive Species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These executive orders establish additional policy obligations (e.g., wetland/floodplain avoidance, environmental justice, cultural resource protection, invasive species prevention) that the agencies considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance and intergovernmental consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: This project is associated with Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance Program Number 20.205, Highway Planning and Construction; the regulations implementing Executive Order 12372 regarding intergovernmental consultation on Federal programs and activities apply to this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies program number and notes intergovernmental consultation requirements under EO 12372 implementing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation for issuance of notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority: 23 U.S.C. 139(l)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory citation is given as the legal authority for publishing the limitation-on-claims notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document headings and drafting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Document headings vary by document type but may contain the agency or agencies that issued and signed a document; the number of the CFR title and the number of each part the document amends, proposes to amend, or is directly related to; the agency docket number / agency internal file number; the RIN which identifies each regulatory action listed in the Unified Agenda of Federal and Deregulatory Actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Document Drafting Handbook for more details; these are expected components when drafting Federal Register documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official vs. prototype/ XML Federal Register legal status
rubrics_metrics.description: The prototype XML-based FederalRegister.gov edition is not an official legal edition and does not provide legal notice or judicial notice; use the official PDF on govinfo.gov for legal research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site aims to present accurate information but users relying on it for legal research should verify results against the official edition; the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register (ACFR) must grant official legal status for XML editions to be authoritative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Inspection statement and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Inspection: The PDF cited is FR Doc. 2024-23691 as it appeared on Public Inspection on 10/11/2024; users should verify contents against a final, official edition of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only official editions provide legal notice to the public and judicial notice to the courts under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.
